sections.h2: Where does a Henry County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Henry County deeds are filed in Napoleon, in Suite 202 up the stairs in the courthouse at 660 N. Perry Street. The county directory lists the Recorder at 419-592-1766 and shows the counter closing at 4:30 on weekdays, with the doors shut on weekends and holidays.

A single recorder serves the whole county, about 416 square miles of land. A farm along the Putnam County line and a house inside Napoleon go through the same window. The county's recorder page calls the office the keeper of real estate records and lists what it takes: deeds, mortgages, mechanic's liens, powers of attorney, IRS liens, subdivision plats, military discharges, partnership papers, and the zoning resolutions of the county and its townships.

The post is elected for four years, in step with the presidential race.

sections.h2: What background on Henry County helps a seller?
sections.html:
Henry County was created in 1820 and organized in 1834, and it takes its name from Patrick Henry. It borders Fulton, Lucas, Wood, Hancock, Putnam, Defiance and Williams Counties in the northwest corner of Ohio. The census counted 262 residents in 1830 and 27,662 in 2020, so deeds here stretch back through two centuries of farm and town sales.

Old chains of title can matter. A house that came through an estate or a long-held farm may carry decades of recorded easements, mortgages and affidavits, and the recorder's index is where a title company finds them. Napoleon serves as both the seat of government and the biggest city.

sections.h2: Which Henry County forms come first?
sections.html:
The Henry County Auditor keeps an office in the same courthouse and answers at 419-592-1956. The auditor's forms page lists the Ohio sale paperwork:

  • DTE 100, the value statement and receipt that goes with a conveyance.
  • DTE 100EX, where you write down why a transfer owes no such fee.
  • DTE 101 for a homestead parcel, DTE 102 for a parcel in the farm valuation program.
  • The Henry County Land Transfer Policy, shown only by title. Ask the auditor's staff for a copy early.

The auditor sees the deed first. Under section 319.202 the buyer files a value statement, the auditor endorses the deed, and a rental house triggers an extra landlord filing under Chapter 5323. Only then does it travel on to the Recorder.

sections.h2: What does the Henry County Auditor charge on a sale?
sections.html:
The auditor's charge comes from section 319.54(G)(3): $1 at minimum, or a dime for each hundred dollars of value if that is more, with part of a hundred counted whole. The seller pays. Get the dollar figure for your price from the counter before closing day.

Any Ohio county may add a transfer tax of up to thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. The grantor pays it before the Recorder sees the deed. Henry County's pages do not say whether the tax is in force, so ask the auditor and see that your closing statement shows the answer.

Several transfers owe no statement fee, among them a deed for no money, a conveyance worth $100 or less, a deed given only as security, and a division among the heirs of one decedent. DTE 100EX is where the reason goes.

sections.h2: What does the Henry County Recorder charge for a deed?
sections.html:
The recorder's page prints no price list, so the figures come from section 317.32. Each charge pairs a base fee with a housing trust fund fee of equal size: $17 each for the first two pages and $4 each for every page after. A county may tack on a preservation surcharge of up to $5. Ask the office for the bottom line on your deed.

Pages are counted at 8.5 by 14 inches, and the caption page is page one. A deed that spills a few lines onto a third sheet costs more, so have it formatted tightly.

The state's layout rule in section 317.114 applies too. Hocking and Highland Counties post a $20 charge for a deed that breaks it. Ask what Henry County adds before you sign one with odd margins or tiny type.

sections.h2: Which Henry County housing figures help set a price?
sections.html:
Census data gives a seller a few local yardsticks. Owners occupy about 82.5% of the occupied homes, and the typical owner-occupied house is valued at $168,600. Only 19 building permits were issued in 2025, so a resale rarely competes with new construction.

About a third of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census and two thirds in rural ones, which explains why farm parcels and big lots show up in the recorder's queue as often as town lots. Transportation and warehousing receipts of roughly $128 million in 2022 set the county apart in the three-county Census table.

sections.h2: How does a sheriff sale reach the Henry County Recorder?
sections.html:
Sheriff sales for orders received after August 1, 2022 run online through RealAuction, and tax sales are held on the first floor of the courthouse. Bidders deposit by wire or ACH, never cash, and the county's page sets deposits by appraised value:

  • $2,000 for an appraisal up to $10,000.
  • $5,000 for an appraisal from $10,000 to $200,000.
  • $10,000 for an appraisal above $200,000.

After the auction the buyer waits 30 to 45 days for the court's confirmation and the sheriff's deed. The former owner keeps title until the judge signs, and the new owner gets title only when the sheriff's deed lands in the Henry County Recorder's index. The judgment creditor and the first lienholder can redeem within 14 days by paying the full price to the clerk of courts.

sections.h2: What property tax help does Henry County offer a seller?
sections.html:
The Treasurer sits in the same courthouse, at P.O. Box 546, Napoleon, phone 419-592-1851. The treasurer's page offers monthly payment plans for unpaid back taxes and current taxes, which halt added interest and penalties. A Tax Installment Prepay plan splits the yearly bill into coupons with no penalty for a late one, provided each half is paid in full by its closing date.

The county reports 40 taxing districts, each with its own rate, and values property at 35% of market. The auditor reappraises every six years and updates in the third. Owners can contest a valuation from January 1 through March 31 before the county Board of Revision, and the 2 1/2% owner-occupancy rollback takes a single application before the first Monday in June.

On the homestead page, the TY2025 figures are a $40,000 income limit and a $28,000 exemption, with more for disabled veterans. A separate page for struggling taxpayers points to NOCAC, the Northwestern Ohio Community Action Commission, and to Maumee Valley Planning's housing program.

faqs.q: Who records Henry County deeds, and where?
faqs.a: The Henry County Recorder, in Suite 202 on the second floor of the courthouse at 660 N. Perry Street in Napoleon. The phone is 419-592-1766.

faqs.q: Do I visit the auditor before the recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer files a statement of value with the auditor, who endorses the deed. The recorder files it after that. Both offices share the courthouse in Napoleon.

faqs.q: How is the Ohio conveyance fee figured?
faqs.a: It is the larger of $1 or ten cents per $100 of value, with any fraction of $100 counted as a full $100. The seller pays it, subject to the statute's exemptions.

faqs.q: Is there a county transfer tax in Henry County?
faqs.a: Call the auditor to find out. State law lets a county charge up to thirty cents per $100 after two hearings, but the county's pages do not state whether Henry County does.

faqs.q: Can a sheriff-sale buyer record immediately?
faqs.a: No. The judge must confirm the sale and the sheriff must receive the deed, which takes 30 to 45 days after the auction. Title passes when the sheriff's deed is recorded.
